questions.question: How do I check the engine oil level correctly?
questions.reference_answer: Engine oil level checking (p83): place the vehicle upright on a level surface; start the engine from cold condition, let it idle for 2 to 3 minutes and stop the engine; wait 2 to 3 minutes for the oil to settle and assess the sight glass (the oil level window is on the right side, p24). questions.question: My coolant looks low. How do I top it up, and which coolant should I use?
questions.reference_answer: Coolant: TOTAL COOLELF AUTO SUPRA -37 ºC; coolant from Total is ready to use and does not require mixing (p21, p87). Expansion tank: fill to max mark - 200 ml (p21). Check coolant level in the expansion tank every 1000 km (or earlier as required) and top up as required (p125). Topping up: remove the radiator expansion tank cap, fill the tank to the upper level line and replace the cap (p87). Full fill/air bleeding (p86-87): vehicle straight on ground level; remove the radiator pressure cap and fill up to the filler neck; air bleed by gently tapping and squeezing both engine-to-radiator hoses and tipping the bike approximately 45-60 degrees left then right, topping back up to the filler neck until the level no longer drops; refit the radiator pressure cap fully tightened clockwise; fill the expansion tank to the upper level line; start in neutral, idle 5 minutes, blip throttle 3 or 4 times, stop and let it cool, top up the expansion tank if required, and check for leaks. NOTE: do not fill coolant with the vehicle on the side stand (p87). WARNING (p86): never open a radiator cap when the engine is hot; released pressure can make coolant boil and spurt out, causing severe burns. WARNING (p87): do not spill coolant; collect it and dispose through authorized agencies; avoid skin contact and wash affected area with soap and water.

questions.question: When removing the battery, which terminal do I disconnect first, and which one goes back on first?

Refitting (p105-107): place the battery in the tray, fix the strap, connect the red positive (+ve) terminal first, then the black negative (-ve) terminal, and refit the seats. NOTE: poor contact or loose fitment of battery terminals may cause ECU failure (p104); clean terminals of corrosion and coat with petroleum jelly (p107). The p11 WARNING notes batteries contain lead, acids and chemicals; exercise extreme caution and wash hands thoroughly after handling. questions.question: How do I check the brake fluid level, and what fluid should I top up with?
questions.reference_answer: Checking brake fluid (p88): place the motorcycle upright on a firm, level surface. Front: check that the reservoir is horizontal and the fluid level is at the center of the window (considered the minimum level). Rear: check that the reservoir is horizontal and the level is between the 'MAX' and 'Min' marks. The pre-ride check says the level must be above the 'MIN' mark (p70). Fluid: DOT 4 (p21). NOTES (p88-89): clean the filler cap before removing; use only DOT 4 brake fluid from sealer container; use only the specified fluid or seals may deteriorate and leak; refill with the same type - adding fluid other than DOT 4 may cause a harmful chemical reaction; keep water and dust out (water lowers the boiling point and may cause vapor lock; dirt may clog ABS hydraulic unit valves). CAUTION (p88): brake fluid is highly corrosive and damages painted parts - clean any spill immediately with a soft (preferably wet) cloth; do not mix DOT 4 and other brake fluid. WARNING (p89): insufficient brake fluid level will cause the brake system to fail; old fluid reduces braking effect; change front and rear fluid per the periodic maintenance schedule (replace at 20,000 km/24 months and 40,000 km/48 months, p127); keep brake fluid out of reach of children and away from skin, eyes and clothing.

CAUTION (p27): gasoline vapour is highly explosive - no flames or sparks, ventilated area only, no smoking while refuelling or with the cap open; wipe off any fuel spilled on painted surfaces immediately as it may leave a permanent stain. questions.question: A fuse blew mid-ride. Can I just bridge it with a bit of wire or foil to get home?
questions.reference_answer: No. WARNING (p112): 'Any attempt to jumper a defective fuse gives rise to the risk of a short-circuit and fire. Always replace a defective fuse with a new fuse of the same rating.' Usage of fuses other than the specified rating, any other conductive materials or low grade fuses will damage the complete electrical system. Instead use a spare: the fuse box holds SF1 Yellow 5 A, SF2 Red 10 A, SF3 Blue 15 A (p112); the fuse carrier is underneath the rider seat (remove pillion and rider seats, p111); a fuse puller is in the tool kit (p81); keep the ignition OFF when replacing fuses (p112). Replace the used spare at the earliest opportunity, and get the electrical system checked and faults corrected immediately after any fuse failure, or fuses may keep failing (p112). Troubleshooting: replace the fuse with same rating; contact an Authorised service center if the problem persists (p121).
